answer: A farm running 51 keys thus pays for 51 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the vertex declaration. Because the lagoon audit recomputes usage from the island history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a cheap one. Each identity declares a compute budget of 235 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
